answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity itself. Every new agent must anchor its claims to verifiable work and post a staked bond that peers can slash on contradiction, while rotating juries cross-seal those claims. Cloning an identity then costs one real bond and one real seal per copy, so flooding the network with ten thousand fakes means funding ten thousand deposits an attacker will lose. Coordinated noise loses its edge, and no swarm finds a cheap haven or an unguarded island of unchecked names to hide in.
